courses.title: A0 — Absolute Beginner
courses.description: Fleng Absolute Beginner: ten sequenced introductory product lessons; not an exam certification course.

lessons.title: Words on the screen
lessons.summary: Follow five short classroom instructions.
goals: Follow five short classroom instructions.
Practise: Imperatives and classroom instructions.
lessons.theory: An instruction tells you what to do. Start with the action word: Read. Listen. Write. Add please to be polite. Use do not, or don't, before an action to say no: Don't write. You do not need a subject in these instructions. Learn each action with its meaning. This is recognition practice, not a pronunciation test.
lessons.reading: Teacher: Open your book, please. Read. Write your name. Student: OK. Teacher: Listen. Don't speak now. Repeat this word, please.
examples: Look at the text. Read it.
Use a pen. Write your name.

lessons.title: Letters and spelling
lessons.summary: Recognise vowels and spell a short name.
goals: Recognise vowels and spell a short name.
Practise: Letter names and spelling chunks.
lessons.theory: English has 26 letters. The vowel letters are a, e, i, o and u; y can also represent a vowel sound. A letter name and its sound in a word are not always the same. Spell a name one letter at a time. Write a capital letter at the start of a name. Use the chunk "How do you spell it?" to ask for letters.
lessons.reading: A: My name is Mia. B: How do you spell it? A: M-I-A. B: Thank you, Mia. This is the English alphabet. Write a small b. Read this page.
examples: Which letter is a vowel? a
Which letter is a consonant? m

lessons.title: A first meeting
lessons.summary: Give a name and greet a new classmate.
goals: Give a name and greet a new classmate.
Practise: I am and you are as introduction chunks.
lessons.grammar: I am and you are as introduction chunks
lessons.theory: Use Hello or Hi when you meet someone. Give your name with "I am" or "My name is". I am can be short: I'm. Say "Nice to meet you" the first time you meet. Reply "Nice to meet you too". Use Goodbye when you leave. Learn these short phrases together. Questions with be will come later.

lessons.title: Numbers zero to twenty
lessons.summary: Read small numbers and give an age.
goals: Read small numbers and give an age.
Practise: Number words and singular age chunks.
lessons.grammar: Number words and singular age chunks
lessons.theory: Learn zero to ten first. Then learn eleven and twelve. Many numbers from thirteen to nineteen end in -teen. Twenty is 20. Use "I am" before your age: I am twenty. Do not say "I have twenty" for your age in English. A phone number is usually read one digit at a time. Use zero for 0 here.

lessons.summary: Name common objects and count them.

Practise: A/an and regular plural -s.
lessons.theory: Use a before a single countable thing that starts with a consonant sound: a bag. Use an before a vowel sound: an apple. It is the sound that matters. For more than one, many nouns add -s: bags. Do not use a or an before a plural noun. Some plurals are different; this lesson uses regular ones only.

lessons.title: People around me
lessons.summary: Match people and things to simple pronouns.
goals: Match people and things to simple pronouns.
Practise: He/she/it/we/they with be.
lessons.theory: I means the speaker. You means the person you speak to. Use he or she for a person who uses that pronoun. Use it for a thing. We includes the speaker and other people. They can mean more than one person. Use am with I, is with he/she/it, and are with you/we/they. This lesson practises plural they.

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.summary: Locate an object in a room.
goals: Locate an object in a room.
Practise: In/on/under and where + be.
lessons.theory: Use in for inside: in a bag. Use on when something touches a surface: on a desk. Use under for a lower position: under a chair. Ask "Where is the key?" for one thing. Ask "Where are the keys?" for more than one. Start with where, then is or are, then the thing.

The cup touches the top of the desk: on the desk.

lessons.theory: Use what you know to make a short exchange. Greet the person. Give your name. Name one thing. Ask where it is. Ask if the other person is ready. Read slowly. lessons.title: My home and possessions
lessons.summary: Describe possessions and who they belong to.
goals: Describe possessions and who they belong to.
Practise: Have/has and possessive adjectives.
lessons.theory: Use have with I, you, we and they. Use has with he, she and it. A possessive adjective comes before a noun: my room, her phone, their garden. It tells us whose thing it is. Do not add an apostrophe to these adjectives. Use his for a male owner and her for a female owner; the object does not choose the adjective.
lessons.reading: I have a flat. My flat has a kitchen and a balcony. My sister has a bicycle. Her bicycle is in our garden. Our home has a small garden. Her bedroom has a blue door. The bathroom is next to my bedroom. We have a sofa in the kitchen.
examples: This phone belongs to me. It is my phone.

lessons.title: A typical weekday
lessons.summary: Describe a daily routine in order.
goals: Describe a daily routine in order.
Practise: Present simple affirmative and third-person -s.
lessons.theory: Use the present simple for things you do regularly. With I, you, we and they, use the base verb: I work. With he, she and it, usually add -s: she works. Add -es after endings such as -sh: he washes. Change consonant + y to -ies: she studies. Use before and after to put actions in order.

goals: Ask about another person’s habits.
Practise: Present simple do/does questions and negatives.
lessons.grammar: Present simple do/does questions and negatives
lessons.theory: Use do or does before the subject in a present-simple question. Does goes with he, she and it. After does, the main verb has no -s: Does she work? Use do not or don't for a negative. Use does not or doesn't with he, she and it. Put usually before the main verb. Put never there too, without adding don't.

Practise: At/on/in for time and clock expressions.
lessons.grammar: At/on/in for time and clock expressions
lessons.theory: Use at with a clock time: at nine o'clock. Use on with a day: on Monday. Use in with a month or part of the day: in July, in the morning. Say quarter past for fifteen minutes after the hour and half past for thirty minutes after. In this lesson, noon is twelve in the day and midnight is twelve at night.
lessons.reading: The class starts at half past nine on Monday. We have a break at quarter past ten. In July, the school opens in the morning only. Please wait for one minute. He works late on Friday. My appointment is at three.

lessons.title: A weekend story
lessons.summary: Tell a sequence of finished past actions.

lessons.grammar: Past simple regular and irregular verbs
lessons.theory: Use the past simple for finished actions. Regular verbs usually add -ed: visited. Common irregular forms must be learned: go/went, buy/bought, eat/ate. Use did plus the base form in questions and didn't plus the base form in negatives. Put events in order with first, then and finally. A past time expression can apply to several following sentences.
lessons.reading: Last Saturday, Lea visited a market. First she bought vegetables. Then she met a friend and ate lunch. She didn't take the bus home; she walked. lessons.summary: Distinguish an intention from a fixed arrangement.

Practise: Going to and present continuous for arrangements.
lessons.grammar: Going to and present continuous for arrangements
lessons.theory: Use be going to plus a base verb for an intention you already have. Use the present continuous for a future arrangement, often with a time and another person involved. Both forms can sometimes fit, so context matters. In these exercises a form is specified when necessary. Use going to for a prediction based on visible evidence: Look at the clouds; it is going to rain.

B: Yes, it is going to rain. What is your plan for tomorrow? There is a dark cloud above the lake. The date is on my calendar.
examples: Use going to: I am going to learn to sail.
Use going to: She is going to book a room.
Use present continuous: We are meeting the instructor tomorrow.

lessons.theory: Use should plus a base verb for advice. Use must or have to for a strong obligation. Mustn't means something is prohibited; don't have to means it is not necessary. lessons.title: When the phone rang
lessons.summary: Describe an ongoing background action and an interruption.
goals: Describe an ongoing background action and an interruption.
Practise: Past continuous and past simple.
lessons.theory: Use was/were plus -ing for an action in progress at a past moment. Use the past simple for a shorter completed event that happened during it. While often introduces the longer background action. When can introduce the interrupting event. The tense describes how you view each action; it is not selected by the conjunction alone.
lessons.reading: I was cooking when the phone rang. My flatmate was studying in the next room. While I was answering the phone, the soup boiled over. We cleaned the cooker and ordered food instead. It was a noisy evening. I was cooking when I got a phone call. Please do not interrupt me. Be careful not to spill the soup.

They were studying when I arrived.
The phone rang while I was cooking. (ring)

lessons.title: If the weather changes
lessons.summary: Explain a realistic future condition and result.
goals: Explain a realistic future condition and result.
Practise: First conditional and future time clauses.
lessons.grammar: First conditional and future time clauses
lessons.theory: For a real future possibility, use if + present simple, then will + base verb: If it rains, we will stay inside. The if clause can come first or second. Do not normally use will in this type of if clause. After when in a future time clause, also use present simple: I will call when I arrive. If means the event is uncertain; when presents it as expected.
lessons.reading: We plan to have a picnic tomorrow. If the weather stays dry, we will meet by the lake. If it rains, we will eat at home. I will send you a message when I leave. Bring a jacket in case it gets cold. Bring a jacket if the weather is wet. The plan has one condition: everyone must agree. The result was clear: we had to cancel the picnic.
examples: If it rains, we will stay inside. (rain)
If it is dry, we will have a picnic.
I will call when I arrive. (arrive)

lessons.theory: A defining relative clause gives information needed to identify a noun. Use who for people and which for things. Use where for places when the clause describes what happens there. lessons.title: Health and practical advice
lessons.summary: Give advice and distinguish it from an obligation.
goals: Give advice and distinguish it from an obligation.
Practise: Should, must and have to.
lessons.theory: Use should plus a base verb for advice. Use must or have to for a strong obligation. Mustn't means something is prohibited; don't have to means it is not necessary. These meanings are different. In a health context, describe symptoms simply and ask a qualified professional for help. This language lesson does not give medical advice.
lessons.reading: A: I feel unwell. B: You should speak to the pharmacist. A: Do I have to make an appointment? B: No, you don't have to book for a simple question. The sign says visitors mustn't smoke inside.
examples: For advice: You should speak to a professional.
It is prohibited: You mustn't smoke here.
It is not necessary: You don't have to book in advance.

exercises.prompt: For advice: You ___ speak to a professional.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: should. For advice: You should speak to a professional. Should, must and have to.

exercises.prompt: It is prohibited: You ___ smoke here.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: mustn't. It is prohibited: You mustn't smoke here. Should, must and have to.

exercises.prompt: It is not necessary: You ___ book in advance.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: don't have to. It is not necessary: You don't have to book in advance. Should, must and have to.

exercises.prompt: She ___ to wear a uniform at work.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: has. She has to wear a uniform at work. Should, must and have to.

exercises.prompt: You should ___ the notice.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: read. You should read the notice. Should, must and have to.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "appointment" in this lesson.
exercises.explanation: In this topic, appointment means запис на прийом.

lessons.title: Getting around a new city
lessons.summary: Follow and give a short route.
goals: Follow and give a short route.
Practise: Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.
lessons.theory: Use imperatives to give directions: Go straight on. Turn left. Cross the road. Use across for movement from one side to another and along for following a road. Past means continuing beyond a landmark. Sequence instructions in short steps. Ask for clarification with "Do you mean this street?" rather than guessing. These route examples practise language only.
lessons.reading: A: Excuse me, how do I get to the bridge? B: Go along this road. Walk past the cinema, then turn right. Go across the square. The bridge is opposite the station. A: So I turn right after the cinema? B: Yes.
examples: Follow this road: walk along it.
From one side of the square to the other: go across it.

exercises.prompt: Follow this road: walk ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: along. Follow this road: walk along it. Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.

exercises.prompt: From one side of the square to the other: go ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: across. From one side of the square to the other: go across it. Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.

exercises.prompt: ___ left at the cinema.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: Turn. Turn left at the cinema. Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.

exercises.prompt: Continue beyond the bank: walk ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: past. Continue beyond the bank: walk past it. Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.

exercises.prompt: Do not turn: go straight ___.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: on. Do not turn: go straight on. Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "turn" in this lesson.
exercises.explanation: In this topic, turn means повертати.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "across" in this lesson.

lessons.title: When the phone rang
lessons.summary: Describe an ongoing background action and an interruption.
goals: Describe an ongoing background action and an interruption.
Practise: Past continuous and past simple.
lessons.theory: Use was/were plus -ing for an action in progress at a past moment. Use the past simple for a shorter completed event that happened during it. While often introduces the longer background action. When can introduce the interrupting event. The tense describes how you view each action; it is not selected by the conjunction alone.
lessons.reading: I was cooking when the phone rang. My flatmate was studying in the next room. While I was answering the phone, the soup boiled over. We cleaned the cooker and ordered food instead. It was a noisy evening.
examples: I was cooking when the phone rang.
They were studying when I arrived.
The phone rang while I was cooking. (ring)

exercises.prompt: I ___ cooking when the phone rang.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: was. I was cooking when the phone rang. Past continuous and past simple.

exercises.prompt: They were ___ when I arrived.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: studying. They were studying when I arrived. Past continuous and past simple.

exercises.prompt: The phone ___ while I was cooking. (ring)
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: rang. The phone rang while I was cooking. (ring) Past continuous and past simple.

exercises.prompt: While she ___ reading, I made tea.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: was. While she was reading, I made tea. Past continuous and past simple.

exercises.prompt: We ___ the cooker afterwards. (clean)
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: cleaned. We cleaned the cooker afterwards. (clean) Past continuous and past simple.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "background" in this lesson.
exercises.explanation: In this topic, background means тло.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "noise" in this lesson.
exercises.explanation: In this topic, noise means шум.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "while" in this lesson.

lessons.title: If the weather changes
lessons.summary: Explain a realistic future condition and result.
goals: Explain a realistic future condition and result.
Practise: First conditional and future time clauses.
lessons.grammar: First conditional and future time clauses
lessons.theory: For a real future possibility, use if + present simple, then will + base verb: If it rains, we will stay inside. The if clause can come first or second. Do not normally use will in this type of if clause. After when in a future time clause, also use present simple: I will call when I arrive. If means the event is uncertain; when presents it as expected.
lessons.reading: We plan to have a picnic tomorrow. If the weather stays dry, we will meet by the lake. If it rains, we will eat at home. I will send you a message when I leave. Bring a jacket in case it gets cold.
examples: If it rains, we will stay inside. (rain)
If it is dry, we will have a picnic.
I will call when I arrive. (arrive)

exercises.prompt: If it ___, we will stay inside. (rain)
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: rains. If it rains, we will stay inside. (rain) First conditional and future time clauses.

exercises.prompt: If it is dry, we ___ have a picnic.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: will. If it is dry, we will have a picnic. First conditional and future time clauses.

exercises.prompt: I will call when I ___. (arrive)
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: arrive. I will call when I arrive. (arrive) First conditional and future time clauses.

exercises.prompt: If she comes, I will ___ her.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: tell. If she comes, I will tell her. First conditional and future time clauses.

exercises.prompt: We will cancel if the lake ___ frozen.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: is. We will cancel if the lake is frozen. First conditional and future time clauses.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "dry" in this lesson.
exercises.explanation: In this topic, dry means сухий.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "message" in this lesson.

lessons.title: Which person do you mean?
lessons.summary: Identify people, things and places precisely.
goals: Identify people, things and places precisely.
Practise: Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.
lessons.theory: A defining relative clause gives information needed to identify a noun. Use who for people and which for things. Use where for places when the clause describes what happens there. Do not put commas around these defining clauses. Compare a person who works here, a tool which opens bottles, and a café where we meet. Keep the verb agreement clear.
lessons.reading: A: Which person is your guide? B: The woman who is holding a green umbrella. A: Is that the café where we meet? B: Yes. Bring the map which is on the table. It shows the path to the museum.
examples: The woman who works here is our guide.
The map which is on the table is mine.
This is the café where we meet.

exercises.prompt: The woman ___ works here is our guide.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: who. The woman who works here is our guide. Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.

exercises.prompt: The map ___ is on the table is mine.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: which. The map which is on the table is mine. Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.

exercises.prompt: This is the café ___ we meet.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: where. This is the café where we meet. Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.

exercises.prompt: A guide is a person ___ helps visitors.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: who. A guide is a person who helps visitors. Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.

exercises.prompt: A key is a thing ___ opens a lock.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: which. A key is a thing which opens a lock. Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "map" in this lesson.
exercises.explanation: In this topic, map means карта.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "identify" in this lesson.

lessons.title: Solving a travel problem
lessons.summary: Explain a travel problem and agree on a solution.
goals: Explain a travel problem and agree on a solution.
Practise: Integrated past, requests and future conditions.
lessons.grammar: Integrated past, requests and future conditions
lessons.theory: Combine past events with a present problem and a future solution. Say what happened using past simple. Explain the result now. Use Could you + base verb for a polite request. Use a first conditional to discuss the next step. A clear service conversation gives the problem, one request and a confirmation; it does not need long or complicated sentences.
lessons.reading: A: I booked a room, but I lost the confirmation. Could you check my name? B: Certainly. What is your surname? A: Novak. B: I have found the booking. If you show your passport, I will give you the key. A: Thank you. Could you also tell me when breakfast starts?
examples: If you show your passport, I will give you the key.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday I ___ my confirmation. (lose)
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: lost. Yesterday I lost my confirmation. (lose) Integrated past, requests and future conditions.

exercises.prompt: Could you ___ my name?
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: check. Could you check my name? Integrated past, requests and future conditions.

exercises.prompt: If you show your passport, I ___ give you the key.
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: will. If you show your passport, I will give you the key. Integrated past, requests and future conditions.

exercises.prompt: I have ___ the booking. (find)
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: found. I have found the booking. (find) Integrated past, requests and future conditions.

exercises.prompt: Could you tell me when breakfast ___?
exercises.explanation: Correct choice: starts. Could you tell me when breakfast starts? Integrated past, requests and future conditions.

lessons.title: Where are you from?
lessons.summary: Say which country you are from and ask a new classmate.
goals: Ask and answer where a person is from.
Use country names and nationality words with a capital letter.
Choose is or are with I, you, he, she, we and they.
lessons.grammar: Where + be + from; country and nationality words
lessons.theory: Ask about a place with Where ... from? Use are with you, we and they, and is with he, she and it: Where are you from? Where is she from? Answer with I am from and a place: I am from Ukraine. A country and its nationality word are two different words: Ukraine and Ukrainian, Poland and Polish. Both always start with a capital letter in English. Use a nationality word after be to describe a person: He is Spanish. Use from before a country or a city: I am from Lviv.
lessons.reading: Hello! My name is Marta. I am from Poland, so I am Polish. My friend Ivan is from Ukraine. He is Ukrainian. Our class is small, but it is a happy class. Our teacher is German. She is from a big city in Germany. Her name is Anna. Today a new student is in our class. Her name is Lucia. She is from Spain. We ask her: Where are you from? She says: I am from Spain, and I am Spanish.
examples: Where are you from? I am from Ukraine.
Where is she from? She is from Poland.
He is Spanish. He is from Spain.
We are German. We are from Germany.

exercises.prompt: Where ___ you from?
exercises.explanation: With you we use are: Where are you from?

exercises.prompt: She ___ from Poland.
exercises.explanation: She is one person, so we use is: She is from Poland.

exercises.prompt: I am from Spain. I am ___.
exercises.explanation: After I am we describe the person with a nationality word: Spanish. Spain is the country.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Every sentence needs a form of be. With he we use is.

exercises.prompt: Ukraine is a ___.
exercises.explanation: Ukraine is the name of a country. Kyiv is a city, and Ukrainian describes a person.

exercises.prompt: Marta is Polish. Where is Marta from?
exercises.explanation: Polish describes the person. The place is Poland.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "country".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "country" means країна.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «місто».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «місто» is city.

exercises.prompt: Which word describes a person?
exercises.explanation: Polish is a nationality word, so it describes a person. Poland is a place. English writes both with a capital letter.

exercises.prompt: A: Where are you from? B: ___
exercises.explanation: Answer with I am from and a place. Ukraine is a place, so it needs from.

practice.prompt: Where ___ they from? (is or are)
practice.explanation: With they we use are: Where are they from?

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: from / is / She / Germany
practice.explanation: The sentence starts with the person, then be, then from and the place.

practice.prompt: Translate into English: «Я з України»
practice.explanation: «Я з України» is I am from Ukraine. You can also say I'm.

practice.prompt: Write two sentences: where you are from and where a friend is from.
practice.model_answer: I am from Ukraine. My friend is from Poland.
practice.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

lessons.title: This, that, these, those
lessons.summary: Point to things that are near and far, one or many.
goals: Use this and these for near things, that and those for far things.
Match this/that with one thing and these/those with more than one.
Write regular and -es plurals such as phones and watches.
lessons.grammar: This / that / these / those with be
lessons.theory: Use this and these for things that are near you. Use that and those for things that are far from you. This and that go with one thing: This is a phone. That is a lamp. These and those go with more than one thing: These are phones. Those are lamps. Remember the pairs: this is, these are; that is, those are. Never say this are. Add -es to a noun that ends in ch, sh or s: one watch, two watches.
lessons.reading: Welcome to my room. This is my bed, and that is my desk by the window. This is a small lamp. Those are my shoes by the door. These are my glasses on the table. That is a big picture on the wall. Is that your jacket? No, it is not my jacket. It is a big jacket for my brother. Please do not move my things. They are all new.
examples: That is a clock on the wall.

vocabulary.example: The laptop is on the desk.
The clock is on the wall.

exercises.prompt: ___ is my laptop. (It is near me.)
exercises.explanation: One thing that is near: this. These is for more than one thing.

exercises.prompt: ___ are my shoes. (They are near me.)
exercises.explanation: Shoes are more than one thing and they are near: these.

exercises.prompt: ___ is a lamp on the wall. (It is far from me.)
exercises.explanation: One thing that is far: that.

exercises.prompt: Look at ___ pictures on the wall over there.
exercises.explanation: Pictures are more than one thing and they are far: those.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: These goes with are. This goes with is.

exercises.prompt: one watch, two ___
exercises.explanation: After ch we add -es: watches.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "towel".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "towel" means рушник.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «тарілка».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «тарілка» is plate.

exercises.prompt: Which word do you use for ONE thing that is FAR from you?
exercises.explanation: That is for one far thing. Those is for more than one far thing.

exercises.prompt: A: Is that your phone? B: ___
exercises.explanation: The question is about one thing, so the short answer uses it is.

practice.prompt: ___ are my glasses. (They are near me.)
practice.explanation: Glasses is plural and near: These are my glasses.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / my / That / jacket
practice.explanation: Start with That, then is, then my jacket.

practice.prompt: Translate into English: «Це мій телефон»
practice.explanation: «Це» for a thing is this (near) or that (far): This is my phone.

practice.prompt: Write two sentences about things near you. Use this and these.
practice.model_answer: This is my phone. These are my shoes.
practice.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

lessons.title: Days and months
lessons.summary: Say the day, the month and when something happens.
goals: Ask and tell the day of the week.
Use on with days and in with months.
Write days and months with a capital letter.
lessons.grammar: On + day, in + month; What day is it today?
lessons.theory: Ask about the day with What day is it today? and answer It is Monday. A week has seven days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. Always write days and months with a capital letter: Monday, May. Use on with a day: on Friday. Use in with a month: in May, in December. Give the month of your birthday: My birthday is in January.
lessons.reading: Today is Monday. My English lesson is on Monday and on Wednesday. On Friday I am with my friends. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. I am free on Sunday. My birthday is in May. My sister is eight. Her birthday is in January. My brother is ten. His birthday is in December. Now I am ready for the week.
examples: What day is it today? It is Friday.
Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

vocabulary.example: Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.
The English class is on Wednesday.
On Friday I am with my friends.

exercises.prompt: My lesson is ___ Friday.
exercises.explanation: Use on with a day: on Friday.

exercises.prompt: My birthday is ___ May.
exercises.explanation: Use in with a month: in May.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Use on with a day, and keep the order: be, then free, then on Sunday.

exercises.prompt: Saturday and Sunday are the ___.
exercises.explanation: The two days after Friday are the weekend.

exercises.prompt: A: What day is it today? B: ___
exercises.explanation: Answer the question with It is and the day. Do not add on here.

exercises.prompt: Monday and Friday are ___ of the week.
exercises.explanation: Monday and Friday are two days of the week.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "month".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "month" means місяць.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «день народження».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «день народження» is birthday.

exercises.prompt: Which month is the first month of the year?
exercises.explanation: The year starts with January and ends with December.

exercises.prompt: A: Is your birthday in May? B: No, ___ in December.
exercises.explanation: Birthday is one thing, so we use it is.

practice.prompt: My English lesson is ___ Wednesday. (on or in)
practice.explanation: Use on with a day: on Wednesday.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / May / in / birthday / My
practice.explanation: Start with My birthday, then is, then in and the month.

practice.prompt: Translate into English: «Сьогодні п’ятниця»
practice.explanation: «Сьогодні п’ятниця» is Today is Friday or It is Friday.

practice.prompt: Write two sentences: one with on and a day, one with in and a month.
practice.model_answer: My lesson is on Friday. My birthday is in May.
practice.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

lessons.title: Numbers and prices
lessons.summary: Count in tens up to a hundred and ask how much things are.
goals: Count in tens from thirty to one hundred.
Ask How much is it? and How much are they?
Say a price with a number and a money word.
lessons.theory: After twenty we count in tens: thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred. Do not mix them up with the -teen numbers: fifteen is 15, but fifty is 50. Ask the price with How much is it? for one thing and How much are they? for more than one thing. Answer with It is or They are and the money word: It is thirty euros. They are fifty dollars. Say one euro but two euros, one dollar but two dollars.
lessons.reading: Welcome to my small shop. The prices are on the wall. The cup is ten euros. The lamp is thirty euros. The shoes are fifty euros. They are not cheap, but they are good. The bag is sixty euros. The phone is one hundred euros. Is it expensive? Not for a good phone! A woman asks: How much is the lamp? I say: It is thirty euros. She says: That is a good price.
examples: How much is it? It is thirty euros.
How much are they? They are fifty dollars.
A cup is cheap. A phone is expensive.

vocabulary.example: The big bag is sixty euros.
The phone is one hundred euros.
The price is on the wall.

exercises.prompt: How much ___ the lamp?
exercises.explanation: The lamp is one thing, so we use is: How much is the lamp?

exercises.prompt: How much ___ the shoes?
exercises.explanation: Shoes are more than one thing, so we use are.

exercises.prompt: Thirty, forty, ___, sixty.
exercises.explanation: We count in tens: thirty, forty, fifty, sixty. Fifteen is 15.

exercises.prompt: The cup is two euros. It is ___.
exercises.explanation: A small price means cheap.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer to "How much is it?"
exercises.explanation: It goes with is. They goes with are.

exercises.prompt: Choose the number word for 100.
exercises.explanation: The number 100 is said one hundred. Ten tens make a hundred.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "price".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "price" means ціна.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «дешевий».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «дешевий» is cheap.

exercises.prompt: Which number is the biggest?
exercises.explanation: Sixty is 60, fifty is 50 and thirty is 30.

exercises.prompt: A: How much are the shoes? B: ___
exercises.explanation: The shoes are more than one thing: They are fifty euros.

practice.prompt: How much ___ the cup? It is ten euros. (is or are)
practice.explanation: The cup is one thing: How much is the cup?

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / much / How / it
practice.explanation: The question starts with How much, then is, then it.

practice.prompt: Translate into English: «Це дорого»
practice.explanation: «Дорого» is expensive: It is expensive.

practice.prompt: Write a price for a cup and a price for a phone.
practice.model_answer: The cup is ten euros. The phone is one hundred euros.
practice.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

lessons.title: At the café
lessons.summary: Order a drink and a snack politely and ask for the bill.
goals: Order food and drink with Can I have ..., please?
Use Here you are and Thank you in the right moment.
Ask for the menu and the bill.
lessons.grammar: Can I have ...? and polite phrases
lessons.theory: Use Can I have ..., please? to ask politely for food and drink. Use a with one thing: a coffee, a cake, a sandwich. For drinks such as water, juice and milk you can also say only the word: Can I have water, please? When someone gives you something, they say Here you are, and you answer Thank you. At the end of the meal ask for the bill: Can I have the bill, please? Ask for the price with How much is it?
lessons.reading: Anna is in a small café. The waiter says: Hello. Here is the menu. Anna says: Thank you. Can I have a coffee and a sandwich, please? The waiter says: Yes. Anything else? Anna says: Can I have a cake, please? The waiter says: Here you are. Anna says: Thank you. Later she asks: Can I have the bill, please? How much is it? The waiter says: It is twelve euros. Anna is happy.
examples: Can I have a coffee, please?
Can I have the menu, please?
Can I have the bill, please?

vocabulary.example: Anna is in a small café.
Can I have a coffee, please?
Can I have the bill, please?

exercises.prompt: Can I ___ a coffee, please?
exercises.explanation: We say Can I have ... to ask politely for something.

exercises.prompt: Someone gives you your tea. You say: ___
exercises.explanation: When you get something, say Thank you.

exercises.prompt: Choose the polite question.

options.text: Can I have the menu, please?

exercises.explanation: Can I have ..., please? is polite. The other two are not complete or polite.

exercises.prompt: At the end you ask for the ___. (It shows the price.)
exercises.explanation: The bill shows how much you must pay. The menu shows what you can order.

exercises.prompt: A: Hello. Here is the menu. B: ___
exercises.explanation: Thank you is the natural answer when someone gives you something.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

options.text: Can I has a sandwich, please?
Can I have a sandwich, please?
Can I am a sandwich, please?

exercises.explanation: After Can I we use the base verb: have.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «сік».

exercises.prompt: Which one is a drink?
exercises.explanation: You drink juice. You eat cake and soup.

exercises.prompt: A: Can I have a tea, please? B: ___
exercises.explanation: The waiter gives you the tea and says Here you are.

practice.prompt: Can I have ___ coffee, please? (a or an)
practice.explanation: Coffee starts with a consonant sound, so we use a: a coffee.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: have / I / Can / the / menu

Can I have a coffee please

data.note: Additive practice for each curriculum lesson. Existing exercises are never changed.

fleng-a0-classroom.prompt: Please ___ your book. (the opposite of close)
fleng-a0-classroom.explanation: Open is the opposite of close: Please open your book.

fleng-a0-classroom.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: the / Listen / to / teacher
fleng-a0-classroom.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb: Listen to the teacher.
«писати» is write in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-classroom.prompt: Write two classroom instructions for a friend. Start each one with a verb.
fleng-a0-classroom.model_answer: Open your book. Repeat the word, please.
fleng-a0-classroom.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-letters.prompt: A, E, I, O and U are ___ letters. (not consonants)
fleng-a0-letters.explanation: A, E, I, O and U are vowel letters; the others are consonants.

fleng-a0-letters.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: your / Spell / please / name
fleng-a0-letters.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb: Spell your name, please.
«слово» is word in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-letters.prompt: Spell your first name letter by letter, with a dash between the letters.
fleng-a0-letters.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-hello.prompt: Hello, I ___ Tom. Nice to meet you.
fleng-a0-hello.explanation: Use am with I: I am Tom (or I'm Tom).

fleng-a0-hello.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: you / Nice / meet / to
fleng-a0-hello.explanation: The set phrase is: Nice to meet you.
«друг» is friend in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-hello.prompt: Introduce yourself in two short sentences: say hello and your name.
fleng-a0-hello.model_answer: Hello! I am Olena. Nice to meet you.
fleng-a0-hello.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-numbers.prompt: Five and five is ___. (write the number as a word)
Put the words in order to make a sentence: years / I / twenty / am / old
fleng-a0-numbers.explanation: Age uses be: I am twenty years old.
«дванадцять» is twelve in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-numbers.prompt: Write your age and the number of people in your family as words.
fleng-a0-numbers.model_answer: I am nineteen. There are four people in my family.
fleng-a0-numbers.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-objects.prompt: I have ___ apple in my bag. (a or an?)
fleng-a0-objects.explanation: Use an before a vowel sound: an apple.

fleng-a0-objects.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / This / a / pencil
fleng-a0-objects.explanation: Statement order: This + is + a + noun.
«ключ» is key in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-objects.prompt: Name three things on your desk. Use a or an with each one.
fleng-a0-objects.model_answer: a pen, an orange and a cup
fleng-a0-objects.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-people.prompt: This is my sister. ___ is a student. (he or she?)
fleng-a0-people.explanation: A sister is a woman, so we say she.

fleng-a0-people.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: are / my / They / parents
fleng-a0-people.explanation: They goes with are: They are my parents.
«брат» is brother in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-people.prompt: Write two sentences about people in your family. Use he, she or they.
fleng-a0-people.model_answer: My mother is a teacher. She is kind.
fleng-a0-people.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-describing.explanation: Червоний is red: My bag is red.

fleng-a0-describing.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: big / a / It / is / house
fleng-a0-describing.explanation: The adjective comes before the noun: a big house.
«старий» is old in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-describing.prompt: Describe one thing in your room with two adjectives.
fleng-a0-describing.model_answer: My chair is black and old.
fleng-a0-describing.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-where.prompt: The cat is ___ the box. (inside it)
fleng-a0-where.explanation: Inside something is in: The cat is in the box.

fleng-a0-where.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: the / Where / keys / are
fleng-a0-where.explanation: Questions with where: Where + are + the keys?
«стіна» is wall in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-where.prompt: Write where two things in your room are. Use in, on or under.
fleng-a0-where.model_answer: My phone is on the table. My bag is under the chair.
fleng-a0-where.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-questions.explanation: Questions with you use Are at the start: Are you tired?

fleng-a0-questions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: not / I / am / late
fleng-a0-questions.explanation: The negative puts not after am: I am not late.
«щасливий» is happy in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-questions.prompt: Write one question with Are you…? and a short answer.
fleng-a0-questions.model_answer: Are you cold? No, I am not.
fleng-a0-questions.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a0-first-day.explanation: This goes with is: This is my classroom.

fleng-a0-first-day.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / notebook / My / the / on / desk
accepted_answers: My notebook is on the desk
fleng-a0-first-day.explanation: Thing + is + place: My notebook is on the desk.
«урок» is lesson in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a0-first-day.prompt: Write two sentences about your first day at a new school or course.
fleng-a0-first-day.model_answer: Today is my first lesson. My partner is friendly.
fleng-a0-first-day.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-possessions.explanation: He, she and it use has: My brother has a new bicycle.

fleng-a1-possessions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: have / We / a / garden / small

fleng-a1-possessions.explanation: «кухня» is kitchen in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-possessions.prompt: Write two sentences about your home. Use have or has and my.
fleng-a1-possessions.model_answer: I have a small flat. My kitchen has a big window.
fleng-a1-possessions.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-routines.explanation: With he/she/it, have becomes has in the present simple.

fleng-a1-routines.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: up / I / at / wake / six
fleng-a1-routines.explanation: Subject + verb + time: I wake up at six.
«вечеря» is dinner in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-routines.prompt: Write three sentences about your weekday morning.
fleng-a1-routines.model_answer: I wake up at seven. I have breakfast. I walk to work.
fleng-a1-routines.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-routine-questions.prompt: ___ he usually take the train? (do or does?)
fleng-a1-routine-questions.explanation: He, she and it use Does in questions.

fleng-a1-routine-questions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: often / go / you / Do / out
fleng-a1-routine-questions.explanation: Question order: Do + you + often + verb.
«завжди» is always in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-routine-questions.prompt: Write one question about a friend's habits and one negative sentence about yours.
fleng-a1-routine-questions.model_answer: Does your friend often cook? I don't take the bus.
fleng-a1-routine-questions.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-time.prompt: The meeting is ___ Monday. (at, on or in?)
fleng-a1-time.explanation: Use on with days: on Monday.

fleng-a1-time.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: at / starts / The / lesson / noon
fleng-a1-time.explanation: Use at with clock times and noon.
«година» is hour in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-time.prompt: Write when you do two things. Use at, on and in.
fleng-a1-time.model_answer: I study at eight. I visit my parents on Sunday and travel in July.
fleng-a1-time.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-town.prompt: There ___ two banks on this street. (is or are?)
Put the words in order to make a sentence: a / near / There / station / is / the / park
accepted_answers: There is a park near the station

fleng-a1-town.explanation: «лікарня» is hospital in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-town.prompt: Write two sentences about places in your town. Use there is and there are.
fleng-a1-town.model_answer: There is a library near my home. There are two parks.
fleng-a1-town.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-food.prompt: How ___ eggs do we need? (much or many?)
fleng-a1-food.explanation: Eggs are countable, so we use many.

fleng-a1-food.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: much / is / How / there / milk
fleng-a1-food.explanation: Milk is uncountable: How much milk is there?
«хліб» is bread in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-food.prompt: Write what is in your kitchen. Use some and any.
fleng-a1-food.model_answer: We have some rice, but we don't have any cheese.
fleng-a1-food.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-abilities.prompt: I ___ swim, but I can't dance. (positive)
fleng-a1-abilities.explanation: Can + verb shows ability: I can swim.

fleng-a1-abilities.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: drive / My / can't / sister

fleng-a1-abilities.explanation: «співати» is sing in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-abilities.prompt: Write two things you can do and one thing you can't do.
fleng-a1-abilities.model_answer: I can cook and draw. I can't play the guitar.
fleng-a1-abilities.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-right-now.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: are / We / for / waiting / bus / the
accepted_answers: We are waiting for the bus

fleng-a1-right-now.explanation: «чекати» is wait in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-right-now.prompt: Write two sentences about what people around you are doing now.
fleng-a1-right-now.model_answer: My brother is reading. I am sitting at my desk.
fleng-a1-right-now.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-likes.explanation: After enjoy, use verb-ing: enjoy listening.

fleng-a1-likes.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: love / They / films / watching

fleng-a1-likes.explanation: «гра» is game in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-likes.prompt: Write about one hobby you like and one activity you don't like. Use -ing.
fleng-a1-likes.model_answer: I love cycling, but I don't like shopping.
fleng-a1-likes.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a1-yesterday.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: at / We / beach / were / the

fleng-a1-yesterday.explanation: «вчора» is yesterday in English. It is one of this lesson's new words.

fleng-a1-yesterday.prompt: Write two sentences about where you were last weekend.
fleng-a1-yesterday.model_answer: I was at home on Saturday. On Sunday I was at the museum.
fleng-a1-yesterday.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

fleng-a2-plans.model_answer: I'm going to study more. I'm seeing my friend on Friday.
