lessons.title: Words on the screen
lessons.summary: Follow five short classroom instructions.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Follow five short classroom instructions.
- Practise: Imperatives and classroom instructions.

## Imperatives and classroom instructions

An instruction tells you what to do. Start with the action word: Read. Listen. Write. Add please to be polite. Use do not, or don't, before an action to say no: Don't write. You do not need a subject in these instructions. Learn each action with its meaning. This is recognition practice, not a pronunciation test.

## Examples

- Look at the text. Read it.
- Use a pen. Write your name.
- Use your ears. Listen.

## Read in context

Teacher: Open your book, please. Read. Write your name. Student: OK. Teacher: Listen. Don't speak now.

## Vocabulary

- read — читати
- listen — слухати
- write — писати
- speak — говорити
- open — відкривати
- close — закривати
- book — книга
- name — ім’я
- please — будь ласка
- repeat — повторювати

lessons.title: Letters and spelling
lessons.summary: Recognise vowels and spell a short name.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Recognise vowels and spell a short name.
- Practise: Letter names and spelling chunks.

## Letter names and spelling chunks

English has 26 letters. The vowel letters are a, e, i, o and u; y can also represent a vowel sound. A letter name and its sound in a word are not always the same. Spell a name one letter at a time. Write a capital letter at the start of a name. Use the chunk "How do you spell it?" to ask for letters.

## Examples

- Which letter is a vowel? a
- Which letter is a consonant? m
- Spell the name Mia: M-I-A.

## Read in context

A: My name is Mia. B: How do you spell it? A: M-I-A. B: Thank you, Mia.

## Vocabulary

- letter — літера
- alphabet — алфавіт
- spell — називати по літерах
- capital — велика літера
- small — маленький
- vowel — голосна літера
- consonant — приголосна літера
- word — слово
- pen — ручка
- page — сторінка

lessons.title: A first meeting
lessons.summary: Give a name and greet a new classmate.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Give a name and greet a new classmate.
- Practise: I am and you are as introduction chunks.

## I am and you are as introduction chunks

Use Hello or Hi when you meet someone. Give your name with "I am" or "My name is". I am can be short: I'm. Say "Nice to meet you" the first time you meet. Reply "Nice to meet you too". Use Goodbye when you leave. Learn these short phrases together. Questions with be will come later.

## Examples

- I am Eva.
- My name is Ben.
- I am = I'm.

## Read in context

A: Hello. I am Eva. B: Hi, Eva. I am Ben. A: Nice to meet you. B: Nice to meet you too. Goodbye!

## Vocabulary

- hello — привіт
- goodbye — до побачення
- morning — ранок
- evening — вечір
- friend — друг
- teacher — учитель
- student — учень
- meet — зустрічати
- welcome — ласкаво просимо
- thanks — дякую

lessons.title: Numbers zero to twenty
lessons.summary: Read small numbers and give an age.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Read small numbers and give an age.
- Practise: Number words and singular age chunks.

## Number words and singular age chunks

Learn zero to ten first. Then learn eleven and twelve. Many numbers from thirteen to nineteen end in -teen. Twenty is 20. Use "I am" before your age: I am twenty. Do not say "I have twenty" for your age in English. A phone number is usually read one digit at a time. Use zero for 0 here.

## Examples

- Write 12 in words. twelve
- Write 20 in words. twenty
- Write 3 in words. three

## Read in context

A: I am twenty. B: I am nineteen. A: My room number is twelve. B: My room is ten.

## Vocabulary

- zero — нуль
- one — один
- two — два
- three — три
- four — чотири
- five — п’ять
- ten — десять
- twelve — дванадцять
- nineteen — дев’ятнадцять
- twenty — двадцять

lessons.title: One thing, two things
lessons.summary: Name common objects and count them.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Name common objects and count them.
- Practise: A/an and regular plural -s.

## A/an and regular plural -s

Use a before a single countable thing that starts with a consonant sound: a bag. Use an before a vowel sound: an apple. It is the sound that matters. For more than one, many nouns add -s: bags. Do not use a or an before a plural noun. Some plurals are different; this lesson uses regular ones only.

## Examples

- an apple
- a bag
- Two pens. (pen)

## Read in context

A: A pen. A bag. An apple. B: Two pens. Three bags. Two apples.

## Vocabulary

- bag — сумка
- apple — яблуко
- desk — письмовий стіл
- chair — стілець
- door — двері
- window — вікно
- cup — чашка
- pencil — олівець
- orange — апельсин
- key — ключ

lessons.title: People around me
lessons.summary: Match people and things to simple pronouns.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Match people and things to simple pronouns.
- Practise: He/she/it/we/they with be.

## He/she/it/we/they with be

I means the speaker. You means the person you speak to. Use he or she for a person who uses that pronoun. Use it for a thing. We includes the speaker and other people. They can mean more than one person. Use am with I, is with he/she/it, and are with you/we/they. This lesson practises plural they.

## Examples

- She is my sister.
- We are students.
- He is my brother.

## Read in context

I am Kim. She is my sister. He is my brother. We are students. They are teachers. It is a photo.

## Vocabulary

- family — сім’я
- sister — сестра
- brother — брат
- mother — мати
- father — батько
- person — людина
- people — люди
- child — дитина
- photo — фотографія
- parent — хтось із батьків

lessons.title: Colours and simple descriptions
lessons.summary: Describe familiar objects with one adjective.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe familiar objects with one adjective.
- Practise: Adjective position and be + adjective.

## Adjective position and be + adjective

An adjective describes a noun. Put it before the noun: a red bag. You can also put it after be: The bag is red. An English adjective does not add -s for plural nouns: two red bags. Use big or small for size, and new or old for age. This lesson uses one adjective at a time.

## Examples

- A red bag. (colour)
- The bag is big.
- Two blue cups. (colour)

## Read in context

The bag is red. It is a big bag. The cups are blue. The book is new.

## Vocabulary

- red — червоний
- blue — синій
- green — зелений
- black — чорний
- white — білий
- big — великий
- old — старий
- new — новий
- yellow — жовтий
- colour — колір

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.summary: Locate an object in a room.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Locate an object in a room.
- Practise: In/on/under and where + be.

## In/on/under and where + be

Use in for inside: in a bag. Use on when something touches a surface: on a desk. Use under for a lower position: under a chair. Ask "Where is the key?" for one thing. Ask "Where are the keys?" for more than one. Start with where, then is or are, then the thing.

## Examples

- The key is inside the bag: in the bag.
- The cup touches the top of the desk: on the desk.
- The ball is below the chair: under the chair.

## Read in context

The key is in the bag. The bag is on the chair. The cup is under the desk. Where is the pen?

## Vocabulary

- in — у
- on — на
- under — під
- here — тут
- there — там
- room — кімната
- box — коробка
- table — стіл
- floor — підлога
- wall — стіна

lessons.title: Yes, no and simple questions
lessons.summary: Ask and answer a short question with be.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Ask and answer a short question with be.
- Practise: Be questions and negatives.

## Be questions and negatives

To ask a question, put am, is or are before the person: Are you ready? For a short answer, use Yes or No plus the pronoun and be: Yes, I am. Add not for a negative: No, I am not. You can say isn't for is not and aren't for are not. Do not use do with these be questions.

## Examples

- Are you ready?
- Is she tired? Yes, she is.
- I am not late.

## Read in context

A: Are you ready? B: Yes, I am. A: Is the room cold? B: No, it is not. It is warm.

## Vocabulary

- ready — готовий
- late — той, хто запізнився
- happy — щасливий
- tired — втомлений
- cold — холодний
- warm — теплий
- yes — так
- no — ні
- question — запитання
- answer — відповідь

lessons.title: My first day: a short exchange
lessons.summary: Understand and complete a short first-day conversation.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Understand and complete a short first-day conversation.
- Practise: Integrated be, articles and location.

## Integrated be, articles and location

Use what you know to make a short exchange. Greet the person. Give your name. Name one thing. Ask where it is. Ask if the other person is ready. Read slowly. Check the subject before you choose am, is or are. Use a or an only with one countable thing. This review combines earlier skills; it introduces no new tense.

## Examples

- I am Ada.
- This is a classroom.
- Where is my notebook?

## Read in context

A: Hello. I am Ada. B: Hi, Ada. I am Tom. A: Is this a classroom? B: Yes, it is. Your seat is here. A: Where is my notebook? B: It is on the desk. A: Thank you. I am ready.

## Vocabulary

- classroom — класна кімната
- seat — місце для сидіння
- notebook — зошит
- school — школа
- lesson — урок
- today — сьогодні
- now — зараз
- partner — партнер
- again — знову
- ok — гаразд

lessons.title: My home and possessions
lessons.summary: Describe possessions and who they belong to.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe possessions and who they belong to.
- Practise: Have/has and possessive adjectives.

## Have/has and possessive adjectives

Use have with I, you, we and they. Use has with he, she and it. A possessive adjective comes before a noun: my room, her phone, their garden. It tells us whose thing it is. Do not add an apostrophe to these adjectives. Use his for a male owner and her for a female owner; the object does not choose the adjective.

## Examples

- She has a bicycle.
- They have a flat.
- This phone belongs to me. It is my phone.

## Read in context

I have a flat. My flat has a kitchen and a balcony. My sister has a bicycle. Her bicycle is in our garden.

## Vocabulary

- home — дім
- flat — квартира
- kitchen — кухня
- bedroom — спальня
- bathroom — ванна кімната
- garden — сад
- phone — телефон
- bicycle — велосипед
- balcony — балкон
- sofa — диван

lessons.title: A typical weekday
lessons.summary: Describe a daily routine in order.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe a daily routine in order.
- Practise: Present simple affirmative and third-person -s.

## Present simple affirmative and third-person -s

Use the present simple for things you do regularly. With I, you, we and they, use the base verb: I work. With he, she and it, usually add -s: she works. Add -es after endings such as -sh: he washes. Change consonant + y to -ies: she studies. Use before and after to put actions in order.

## Examples

- She works at home. (work)
- I eat breakfast at seven. (eat)
- He studies English. (study)

## Read in context

I get up at seven. I eat breakfast and walk to work. My sister gets up at eight. She studies at home. We cook dinner after work.

## Vocabulary

- wake up — прокидатися
- breakfast — сніданок
- work — працювати
- study — навчатися
- walk — ходити пішки
- cook — готувати їжу
- dinner — вечеря
- sleep — спати
- wash — мити
- weekday — будній день

lessons.title: Asking about habits
lessons.summary: Ask about another person’s habits.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Ask about another person’s habits.
- Practise: Present simple do/does questions and negatives.

## Present simple do/does questions and negatives

Use do or does before the subject in a present-simple question. Does goes with he, she and it. After does, the main verb has no -s: Does she work? Use do not or don't for a negative. Use does not or doesn't with he, she and it. Put usually before the main verb. Put never there too, without adding don't.

## Examples

- Do you take the bus?
- Does she work early?
- He doesn't take the train. (negative)

## Read in context

A: Do you usually take the bus? B: No, I don't. I walk. A: Does your brother walk too? B: No, he doesn't. He takes the train.

## Vocabulary

- usually — зазвичай
- often — часто
- sometimes — іноді
- never — ніколи
- always — завжди
- bus — автобус
- train — поїзд
- weekend — вихідні
- habit — звичка
- early — рано

lessons.title: Time and schedules
lessons.summary: Read a simple timetable and state meeting times.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Read a simple timetable and state meeting times.
- Practise: At/on/in for time and clock expressions.

## At/on/in for time and clock expressions

Use at with a clock time: at nine o'clock. Use on with a day: on Monday. Use in with a month or part of the day: in July, in the morning. Say quarter past for fifteen minutes after the hour and half past for thirty minutes after. In this lesson, noon is twelve in the day and midnight is twelve at night.

## Examples

- The lesson starts at nine o'clock.
- We meet on Monday.
- The course starts in July.

## Read in context

The class starts at half past nine on Monday. We have a break at quarter past ten. In July, the school opens in the morning only.

## Vocabulary

- hour — година
- minute — хвилина
- monday — понеділок
- friday — п’ятниця
- july — липень
- noon — полудень
- midnight — північ
- break — перерва
- timetable — розклад
- appointment — зустріч за домовленістю

lessons.title: Places in my town
lessons.summary: Describe local places and ask what is nearby.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe local places and ask what is nearby.
- Practise: There is/are and some/any.

## There is/are and some/any

Use there is with one thing and there are with plural things. Use Is there or Are there to ask. Use some in many positive plural sentences: There are some shops. Use any in neutral questions and negatives: Are there any shops? There aren't any banks. There describes existence; it does not mean the same as they.

## Examples

- There is a library.
- There are two banks.
- Is there a station?

## Read in context

There is a library near my flat. There are some shops next to it. Is there a station? Yes, there is. There aren't any hotels in this street.

## Vocabulary

- library — бібліотека
- shop — магазин
- bank — банк
- station — станція
- hotel — готель
- street — вулиця
- park — парк
- hospital — лікарня
- near — біля
- next to — поруч із

lessons.title: Food and simple quantities
lessons.summary: Ask for food using appropriate quantity words.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Ask for food using appropriate quantity words.
- Practise: Countable/uncountable nouns and much/many.

## Countable/uncountable nouns and much/many

Countable nouns have singular and plural forms: an egg, two eggs. Uncountable nouns such as rice and water do not normally take a/an or a plural -s. Use some rice or a bottle of water. Ask how many with plural countable nouns and how much with uncountable nouns. A loaf of bread is countable; bread on its own is uncountable.

## Examples

- How many eggs do we need?
- How much water is there?
- I'd like some rice.

## Read in context

A: How many eggs do we need? B: Two. A: How much rice? B: A little rice and some bread. A: Is there any water? B: Yes, a bottle.

## Vocabulary

- egg — яйце
- rice — рис
- bread — хліб
- water — вода
- milk — молоко
- cheese — сир
- bottle — пляшка
- loaf — буханець
- potato — картоплина
- tomato — помідор

lessons.title: What can you do?
lessons.summary: Describe abilities and ask about a partner’s skills.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe abilities and ask about a partner’s skills.
- Practise: Can/cannot for ability.

## Can/cannot for ability

Use can before the base verb for an ability: I can swim. The form stays the same for every subject: she can swim too. Do not add to or -s after can. For a negative, use cannot or can't. Put can before the subject for a question: Can you drive? Answer Yes, I can or No, I can't.

## Examples

- She can swim well.
- Can you drive?
- He can't sing. (not able)

## Read in context

I can swim, but I can't drive. My friend can drive. Can she dance? Yes, she can. We can both sing.

## Vocabulary

- swim — плавати
- drive — керувати автомобілем
- dance — танцювати
- sing — співати
- run — бігати
- draw — малювати
- skill — навичка
- guitar — гітара
- fast — швидко
- well — добре

lessons.title: What is happening now?
lessons.summary: Describe actions happening at the moment.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe actions happening at the moment.
- Practise: Present continuous affirmative and negative.

## Present continuous affirmative and negative

Use am/is/are plus an -ing verb for an action happening now: I am reading. Add not after be for a negative. Ask by moving be before the subject. For most verbs, add -ing. Drop a final silent e: make becomes making. Some short verbs double the last consonant: run becomes running. Time expressions such as right now help show the meaning.

## Examples

- I am reading now.
- She is making tea. (make)
- They are talking.

## Read in context

It is raining. I am sitting in a café. The waiter is making tea. Two people are talking. My friend is not working today; she is reading.

## Vocabulary

- rain — дощити
- sit — сидіти
- waiter — офіціант
- café — кафе
- tea — чай
- talk — розмовляти
- make — робити
- wait — чекати
- wear — носити одяг
- coat — пальто

lessons.title: Free time and preferences
lessons.summary: Explain simple leisure preferences.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Explain simple leisure preferences.
- Practise: Like/love/enjoy + -ing and simple contrast.

## Like/love/enjoy + -ing and simple contrast

After enjoy, use an -ing form: I enjoy reading. Like and love can also take -ing forms when you talk about an activity in general. Use but to contrast two ideas and because to give a reason. Keep the subject and verb in each clause: I like walking because it is relaxing. Use don't or doesn't to make a present-simple negative.

## Examples

- I enjoy reading books.
- She doesn't like shopping. (negative)
- I like walking because it is relaxing. (reason)

## Read in context

I enjoy cycling, but my brother likes painting. We both love listening to music. I don't like shopping because it is tiring. At weekends we meet friends.

## Vocabulary

- cycling — їзда на велосипеді
- painting — малювання фарбами
- music — музика
- shopping — покупки
- relaxing — розслаблюючий
- tiring — виснажливий
- hobby — хобі
- film — фільм
- game — гра
- free time — вільний час

lessons.title: Where were you yesterday?
lessons.summary: Describe a past location and state.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe a past location and state.
- Practise: Past simple of be.

## Past simple of be

Use was with I, he, she and it for the past of be. Use were with you, we and they. Add not for a negative: wasn't or weren't. Move was/were before the subject for questions. Yesterday and last night show finished past time. Do not use did with be. This lesson describes states and places; other past verbs come next.

## Examples

- I was at the museum yesterday.
- They were at the beach last night.
- Was she at home yesterday?

## Read in context

Yesterday I was at the museum. My friends were at the beach. The weather was sunny. We weren't at school. Were you at home? No, I wasn't.

## Vocabulary

- yesterday — вчора
- museum — музей
- beach — пляж
- sunny — сонячний
- cloudy — хмарний
- last night — минулої ночі
- trip — поїздка
- weather — погода
- busy — зайнятий
- quiet — тихий

lessons.title: A weekend story
lessons.summary: Tell a sequence of finished past actions.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Tell a sequence of finished past actions.
- Practise: Past simple regular and irregular verbs.

## Past simple regular and irregular verbs

Use the past simple for finished actions. Regular verbs usually add -ed: visited. Common irregular forms must be learned: go/went, buy/bought, eat/ate. Use did plus the base form in questions and didn't plus the base form in negatives. Put events in order with first, then and finally. A past time expression can apply to several following sentences.

## Examples

- Yesterday she bought vegetables. (buy)
- Did he visit the market?
- We didn't take the bus.

## Read in context

Last Saturday, Lea visited a market. First she bought vegetables. Then she met a friend and ate lunch. She didn't take the bus home; she walked. "Did you enjoy the market?" her friend asked. "Yes, I did," she said.

## Vocabulary

- market — ринок
- vegetable — овоч
- visit — відвідувати
- buy — купувати
- spend — витрачати
- arrive — прибувати
- leave — залишати
- finally — нарешті
- ticket — квиток
- journey — подорож

lessons.title: Choosing a place to stay
lessons.summary: Compare accommodation using clear criteria.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Compare accommodation using clear criteria.
- Practise: Comparatives and superlatives.

## Comparatives and superlatives

For many short adjectives, add -er to compare two things and -est for the highest degree in a group. Use than after a comparative: cheaper than. Use the before a superlative: the cheapest. For longer adjectives, use more and most. Good becomes better and best. State the group when it matters: the best hotel of these three.

## Examples

- This hostel is cheaper than that hotel. (cheap)
- Of these three, this room is the smallest. (small)
- This bed is more comfortable than that one.

## Read in context

The hostel is cheaper than the hotel, but the hotel is quieter. The apartment is more comfortable than the hostel. Of the three, the hotel is the most expensive. We choose the apartment because it has the best kitchen.

## Vocabulary

- hostel — хостел
- apartment — квартира для проживання
- cheap — дешевий
- expensive — дорогий
- comfortable — зручний
- price — ціна
- clean — чистий
- safe — безпечний
- distance — відстань
- choice — вибір

lessons.title: Plans and arrangements
lessons.summary: Distinguish an intention from a fixed arrangement.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Distinguish an intention from a fixed arrangement.
- Practise: Going to and present continuous for arrangements.

## Going to and present continuous for arrangements

Use be going to plus a base verb for an intention you already have. Use the present continuous for a future arrangement, often with a time and another person involved. Both forms can sometimes fit, so context matters. In these exercises a form is specified when necessary. Use going to for a prediction based on visible evidence: Look at the clouds; it is going to rain.

## Examples

- Use going to: I am going to learn to sail.
- Use going to: She is going to book a room.
- Use present continuous: We are meeting the instructor tomorrow.

## Read in context

A: What are you going to do this summer? B: I am going to learn to sail. I am meeting the instructor at ten tomorrow; we booked it yesterday. A: Look at those dark clouds. B: Yes, it is going to rain.

## Vocabulary

- arrangement — домовленість
- plan — план
- summer — літо
- instructor — інструктор
- book — бронювати
- sail — ходити під вітрилом
- tomorrow — завтра
- cloud — хмара
- intention — намір
- calendar — календар

lessons.title: Experiences and recent results
lessons.summary: Ask about experiences without giving a finished past time.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Ask about experiences without giving a finished past time.
- Practise: Present perfect with ever/never/already/yet.

## Present perfect with ever/never/already/yet

Build the present perfect with have/has plus a past participle: have seen, has finished. Use it for life experience without a finished past time or for a result relevant now. Ever often appears in questions; never means at no time. Already commonly appears before the participle; yet often comes at the end of a question or negative. Use past simple with yesterday.

## Examples

- Have you ever seen a mountain? (see)
- She has already finished.
- I haven't booked a session yet.

## Read in context

A: Have you ever tried climbing? B: Yes, I have. I tried it last summer. A: Have you booked another session yet? B: No, I haven't. My friend has already booked one, but I have never climbed indoors.

## Vocabulary

- climbing — скелелазіння
- experience — досвід
- already — вже
- yet — ще
- ever — коли-небудь
- indoors — у приміщенні
- session — заняття
- finish — закінчувати
- try — пробувати
- recently — нещодавно

lessons.title: Health and practical advice
lessons.summary: Give advice and distinguish it from an obligation.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Give advice and distinguish it from an obligation.
- Practise: Should, must and have to.

## Should, must and have to

Use should plus a base verb for advice. Use must or have to for a strong obligation. Mustn't means something is prohibited; don't have to means it is not necessary. These meanings are different. In a health context, describe symptoms simply and ask a qualified professional for help. This language lesson does not give medical advice.

## Examples

- For advice: You should speak to a professional.
- It is prohibited: You mustn't smoke here.
- It is not necessary: You don't have to book in advance.

## Read in context

A: I feel unwell. B: You should speak to the pharmacist. A: Do I have to make an appointment? B: No, you don't have to book for a simple question. The sign says visitors mustn't smoke inside.

## Vocabulary

- headache — головний біль
- symptom — симптом
- appointment — запис на прийом
- pharmacist — фармацевт
- rest — відпочинок
- advice — порада
- obligation — обов’язок
- necessary — необхідний
- prohibited — заборонений
- unwell — нездужий

lessons.title: Getting around a new city
lessons.summary: Follow and give a short route.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Follow and give a short route.
- Practise: Directional imperatives and movement prepositions.

## Directional imperatives and movement prepositions

Use imperatives to give directions: Go straight on. Turn left. Cross the road. Use across for movement from one side to another and along for following a road. Past means continuing beyond a landmark. Sequence instructions in short steps. Ask for clarification with "Do you mean this street?" rather than guessing. These route examples practise language only.

## Examples

- Follow this road: walk along it.
- From one side of the square to the other: go across it.
- Turn left at the cinema.

## Read in context

A: Excuse me, how do I get to the bridge? B: Go along this road. Walk past the cinema, then turn right. Go across the square. The bridge is opposite the station. A: So I turn right after the cinema? B: Yes.

## Vocabulary

- bridge — міст
- square — площа
- cinema — кінотеатр
- opposite — навпроти
- straight — прямо
- turn — повертати
- cross — перетинати
- along — уздовж
- across — через
- landmark — орієнтир

lessons.title: When the phone rang
lessons.summary: Describe an ongoing background action and an interruption.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Describe an ongoing background action and an interruption.
- Practise: Past continuous and past simple.

## Past continuous and past simple

Use was/were plus -ing for an action in progress at a past moment. Use the past simple for a shorter completed event that happened during it. While often introduces the longer background action. When can introduce the interrupting event. The tense describes how you view each action; it is not selected by the conjunction alone.

## Examples

- I was cooking when the phone rang.
- They were studying when I arrived.
- The phone rang while I was cooking. (ring)

## Read in context

I was cooking when the phone rang. My flatmate was studying in the next room. While I was answering the phone, the soup boiled over. We cleaned the cooker and ordered food instead. It was a noisy evening.

## Vocabulary

- phone call — телефонний дзвінок
- interrupt — переривати
- background — тло
- soup — суп
- cooker — кухонна плита
- noise — шум
- spill — розливати
- ring — дзвонити
- while — поки
- instead — натомість

lessons.title: If the weather changes
lessons.summary: Explain a realistic future condition and result.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Explain a realistic future condition and result.
- Practise: First conditional and future time clauses.

## First conditional and future time clauses

For a real future possibility, use if + present simple, then will + base verb: If it rains, we will stay inside. The if clause can come first or second. Do not normally use will in this type of if clause. After when in a future time clause, also use present simple: I will call when I arrive. If means the event is uncertain; when presents it as expected.

## Examples

- If it rains, we will stay inside. (rain)
- If it is dry, we will have a picnic.
- I will call when I arrive. (arrive)

## Read in context

We plan to have a picnic tomorrow. If the weather stays dry, we will meet by the lake. If it rains, we will eat at home. I will send you a message when I leave. Bring a jacket in case it gets cold.

## Vocabulary

- picnic — пікнік
- lake — озеро
- dry — сухий
- wet — мокрий
- jacket — куртка
- message — повідомлення
- condition — умова
- result — результат
- forecast — прогноз
- cancel — скасовувати

lessons.title: Which person do you mean?
lessons.summary: Identify people, things and places precisely.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Identify people, things and places precisely.
- Practise: Defining relative clauses with who/which/where.

## Defining relative clauses with who/which/where

A defining relative clause gives information needed to identify a noun. Use who for people and which for things. Use where for places when the clause describes what happens there. Do not put commas around these defining clauses. Compare a person who works here, a tool which opens bottles, and a café where we meet. Keep the verb agreement clear.

## Examples

- The woman who works here is our guide.
- The map which is on the table is mine.
- This is the café where we meet.

## Read in context

A: Which person is your guide? B: The woman who is holding a green umbrella. A: Is that the café where we meet? B: Yes. Bring the map which is on the table. It shows the path to the museum.

## Vocabulary

- guide — гід
- umbrella — парасоля
- map — карта
- path — стежка
- tool — інструмент
- identify — ідентифікувати
- describe — описувати
- hold — тримати
- entrance — вхід
- visitor — відвідувач

lessons.title: Solving a travel problem
lessons.summary: Explain a travel problem and agree on a solution.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Explain a travel problem and agree on a solution.
- Practise: Integrated past, requests and future conditions.

## Integrated past, requests and future conditions

Combine past events with a present problem and a future solution. Say what happened using past simple. Explain the result now. Use Could you + base verb for a polite request. Use a first conditional to discuss the next step. A clear service conversation gives the problem, one request and a confirmation; it does not need long or complicated sentences.

## Examples

- Yesterday I lost my confirmation. (lose)
- Could you check my name?
- If you show your passport, I will give you the key.

## Read in context

A: I booked a room, but I lost the confirmation. Could you check my name? B: Certainly. What is your surname? A: Novak. B: I have found the booking. If you show your passport, I will give you the key. A: Thank you. Could you also tell me when breakfast starts?

## Vocabulary

- booking — бронювання
- confirmation — підтвердження
- surname — прізвище
- passport — паспорт
- reception — стійка реєстрації
- delay — затримка
- luggage — багаж
- receipt — квитанція
- solution — рішення
- available — доступний

courses.title: English Foundations
courses.description: Start from zero: greetings, the verb to be, and everyday numbers and dates.

lessons.title: Greetings and introductions
lessons.summary: Say hello, introduce yourself and say goodbye politely.
lessons.theory:
## Saying hello

Use "Hello" in most situations and "Hi" with friends. In the morning you can
say "Good morning".

- Hello, my name is Alex.
- Hi, I'm Sam. Nice to meet you.
- Good morning, Mrs Brown.

## Introducing yourself

To give your name, use "My name is ..." or "I'm ...". To ask, say "What's your
name?".

When you meet someone for the first time, add "Nice to meet you". The usual
reply is "Nice to meet you too".

## Saying goodbye

- Goodbye. See you tomorrow.
- Bye! Have a nice day.
- See you later.

lessons.title: The verb "to be"
lessons.summary: Use am, is and are to describe people and things.
lessons.theory:
## The verb "to be"

The verb "to be" has three forms in the present: am, is and are. Use "am" with
I, "is" with he, she and it, and "are" with you, we and they.

- I am a student.
- She is from Spain.
- We are ready.

## Short forms

In speech we usually use short forms: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're,
they're.

- I'm tired.
- They're at home.

## Negative sentences and questions

Add "not" after the verb for the negative. Move the verb to the front for a
question.

- I am not late.
- Are you a teacher?
- Is she your sister?

lessons.title: Numbers, days and dates
lessons.summary: Count to one hundred and talk about the days of the week.
lessons.theory:
## Numbers

Learn the numbers from one to twenty first, then the tens: twenty, thirty,
forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety and one hundred.

- 1 one, 2 two, 3 three
- 10 ten, 11 eleven, 12 twelve
- 20 twenty, 30 thirty

## Days of the week

- Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday
- Thursday, Friday
- Saturday, Sunday

## Saying dates

In British English the day comes before the month: "the third of May". In
American English the month comes first: "May third".

- My birthday is on the first of June.
- The meeting is on Friday.

## Ordinal numbers

Dates use ordinal numbers: first, second, third, fourth, fifth, then add
"-th" to most others: sixth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth, twentieth.

- the first of June
- the eleventh of October

lessons.title: Where are you from?
lessons.summary: Say which country you are from and ask a new classmate.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Ask and answer where a person is from.
- Use country names and nationality words with a capital letter.
- Choose is or are with I, you, he, she, we and they.

## Where + be + from; country and nationality words

Ask about a place with Where ... from? Use are with you, we and they, and is with he, she and it: Where are you from? Where is she from? Answer with I am from and a place: I am from Ukraine. A country and its nationality word are two different words: Ukraine and Ukrainian, Poland and Polish. Both always start with a capital letter in English. Use a nationality word after be to describe a person: He is Spanish. Use from before a country or a city: I am from Lviv.

## Examples

- Where are you from? I am from Ukraine.
- Where is she from? She is from Poland.
- He is Spanish. He is from Spain.
- We are German. We are from Germany.

## Read in context

Hello! My name is Marta. I am from Poland, so I am Polish. My friend Ivan is from Ukraine. He is Ukrainian. Our class is small, but it is a happy class. Our teacher is German. She is from a big city in Germany. Her name is Anna. Today a new student is in our class. Her name is Lucia. She is from Spain. We ask her: Where are you from? She says: I am from Spain, and I am Spanish.

## Vocabulary

- country — країна
- city — місто
- from — з, родом із
- ukraine — Україна
- ukrainian — український; українець
- poland — Польща
- polish — польський; поляк
- germany — Німеччина
- german — німецький; німець
- spain — Іспанія
- spanish — іспанський; іспанець
- american — американський; американець

lessons.title: This, that, these, those
lessons.summary: Point to things that are near and far, one or many.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Use this and these for near things, that and those for far things.
- Match this/that with one thing and these/those with more than one.
- Write regular and -es plurals such as phones and watches.

## This / that / these / those with be

Use this and these for things that are near you. Use that and those for things that are far from you. This and that go with one thing: This is a phone. That is a lamp. These and those go with more than one thing: These are phones. Those are lamps. Remember the pairs: this is, these are; that is, those are. Never say this are. Add -es to a noun that ends in ch, sh or s: one watch, two watches.

## Examples

- This is my phone.
- That is a clock on the wall.
- These are my shoes.
- Those are your glasses.

## Read in context

Welcome to my room. This is my bed, and that is my desk by the window. This is a small lamp. Those are my shoes by the door. These are my glasses on the table. That is a big picture on the wall. Is that your jacket? No, it is not my jacket. It is a big jacket for my brother. Please do not move my things. They are all new.

## Vocabulary

- phone — телефон
- laptop — ноутбук
- shoe — черевик, взуття
- watch — наручний годинник
- picture — картина, малюнок
- clock — настінний годинник
- lamp — лампа
- plate — тарілка
- towel — рушник
- bed — ліжко
- jacket — куртка
- glasses — окуляри

lessons.title: Days and months
lessons.summary: Say the day, the month and when something happens.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Ask and tell the day of the week.
- Use on with days and in with months.
- Write days and months with a capital letter.

## On + day, in + month; What day is it today?

Ask about the day with What day is it today? and answer It is Monday. A week has seven days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. Always write days and months with a capital letter: Monday, May. Use on with a day: on Friday. Use in with a month: in May, in December. Give the month of your birthday: My birthday is in January.

## Examples

- What day is it today? It is Friday.
- My lesson is on Wednesday.
- My birthday is in May.
- Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

## Read in context

Today is Monday. My English lesson is on Monday and on Wednesday. On Friday I am with my friends. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. I am free on Sunday. My birthday is in May. My sister is eight. Her birthday is in January. My brother is ten. His birthday is in December. Now I am ready for the week.

## Vocabulary

- day — день
- week — тиждень
- weekend — вихідні
- month — місяць
- birthday — день народження
- monday — понеділок
- wednesday — середа
- friday — п’ятниця
- sunday — неділя
- january — січень
- may — травень
- december — грудень

lessons.title: Numbers and prices
lessons.summary: Count in tens up to a hundred and ask how much things are.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Count in tens from thirty to one hundred.
- Ask How much is it? and How much are they?
- Say a price with a number and a money word.

## Numbers 30-100; How much is/are ...?

After twenty we count in tens: thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred. Do not mix them up with the -teen numbers: fifteen is 15, but fifty is 50. Ask the price with How much is it? for one thing and How much are they? for more than one thing. Answer with It is or They are and the money word: It is thirty euros. They are fifty dollars. Say one euro but two euros, one dollar but two dollars.

## Examples

- How much is it? It is thirty euros.
- How much are they? They are fifty dollars.
- A cup is cheap. A phone is expensive.
- Thirty, forty, fifty, sixty.

## Read in context

Welcome to my small shop. The prices are on the wall. The cup is ten euros. The lamp is thirty euros. The shoes are fifty euros. They are not cheap, but they are good. The bag is sixty euros. The phone is one hundred euros. Is it expensive? Not for a good phone! A woman asks: How much is the lamp? I say: It is thirty euros. She says: That is a good price.

## Vocabulary

- thirty — тридцять
- forty — сорок
- fifty — п’ятдесят
- sixty — шістдесят
- hundred — сто
- price — ціна
- cheap — дешевий
- expensive — дорогий
- dollar — долар
- euro — євро
- money — гроші
- shop — магазин

lessons.title: At the café
lessons.summary: Order a drink and a snack politely and ask for the bill.
lessons.theory:
## Learning goals

- Order food and drink with Can I have ..., please?
- Use Here you are and Thank you in the right moment.
- Ask for the menu and the bill.

## Can I have ...? and polite phrases

Use Can I have ..., please? to ask politely for food and drink. Use a with one thing: a coffee, a cake, a sandwich. For drinks such as water, juice and milk you can also say only the word: Can I have water, please? When someone gives you something, they say Here you are, and you answer Thank you. At the end of the meal ask for the bill: Can I have the bill, please? Ask for the price with How much is it?

## Examples

- Can I have a coffee, please?
- Can I have the menu, please?
- Here you are. - Thank you.
- Can I have the bill, please?

## Read in context

Anna is in a small café. The waiter says: Hello. Here is the menu. Anna says: Thank you. Can I have a coffee and a sandwich, please? The waiter says: Yes. Anything else? Anna says: Can I have a cake, please? The waiter says: Here you are. Anna says: Thank you. Later she asks: Can I have the bill, please? How much is it? The waiter says: It is twelve euros. Anna is happy.

## Vocabulary

- café — кав’ярня
- coffee — кава
- tea — чай
- water — вода
- juice — сік
- milk — молоко
- sandwich — бутерброд
- cake — торт, тістечко
- soup — суп
- menu — меню
- bill — рахунок
- waiter — офіціант

exercises.prompt: Where ___ you from?
exercises.explanation: With you we use are: Where are you from?

exercises.prompt: She ___ from Poland.
exercises.explanation: She is one person, so we use is: She is from Poland.

exercises.prompt: I am from Spain. I am ___.
exercises.explanation: After I am we describe the person with a nationality word: Spanish. Spain is the country.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Every sentence needs a form of be. With he we use is.

exercises.prompt: Ukraine is a ___.
exercises.explanation: Ukraine is the name of a country. Kyiv is a city, and Ukrainian describes a person.

exercises.prompt: Marta is Polish. Where is Marta from?
exercises.explanation: Polish describes the person. The place is Poland.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "country".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "country" means країна.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «місто».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «місто» is city.

exercises.prompt: Which word describes a person?
exercises.explanation: Polish is a nationality word, so it describes a person. Poland is a place. English writes both with a capital letter.

exercises.prompt: A: Where are you from? B: ___
exercises.explanation: Answer with I am from and a place. Ukraine is a place, so it needs from.

exercises.prompt: Where ___ they from? (is or are)
exercises.explanation: With they we use are: Where are they from?

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: from / is / She / Germany
exercises.explanation: The sentence starts with the person, then be, then from and the place.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: «Я з України»
exercises.explanation: «Я з України» is I am from Ukraine. You can also say I'm.

exercises.prompt: Write two sentences: where you are from and where a friend is from.
exercises.model_answer: I am from Ukraine. My friend is from Poland.
exercises.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

exercises.prompt: ___ is my laptop. (It is near me.)
exercises.explanation: One thing that is near: this. These is for more than one thing.

exercises.prompt: ___ are my shoes. (They are near me.)
exercises.explanation: Shoes are more than one thing and they are near: these.

exercises.prompt: ___ is a lamp on the wall. (It is far from me.)
exercises.explanation: One thing that is far: that.

exercises.prompt: Look at ___ pictures on the wall over there.
exercises.explanation: Pictures are more than one thing and they are far: those.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: These goes with are. This goes with is.

exercises.prompt: one watch, two ___
exercises.explanation: After ch we add -es: watches.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "towel".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "towel" means рушник.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «тарілка».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «тарілка» is plate.

exercises.prompt: Which word do you use for ONE thing that is FAR from you?
exercises.explanation: That is for one far thing. Those is for more than one far thing.

exercises.prompt: A: Is that your phone? B: ___
exercises.explanation: The question is about one thing, so the short answer uses it is.

exercises.prompt: ___ are my glasses. (They are near me.)
exercises.explanation: Glasses is plural and near: These are my glasses.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / my / That / jacket
exercises.explanation: Start with That, then is, then my jacket.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: «Це мій телефон»
exercises.explanation: «Це» for a thing is this (near) or that (far): This is my phone.

exercises.prompt: Write two sentences about things near you. Use this and these.
exercises.model_answer: This is my phone. These are my shoes.
exercises.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

exercises.prompt: My lesson is ___ Friday.
exercises.explanation: Use on with a day: on Friday.

exercises.prompt: My birthday is ___ May.
exercises.explanation: Use in with a month: in May.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Use on with a day, and keep the order: be, then free, then on Sunday.

exercises.prompt: Saturday and Sunday are the ___.
exercises.explanation: The two days after Friday are the weekend.

exercises.prompt: A: What day is it today? B: ___
exercises.explanation: Answer the question with It is and the day. Do not add on here.

exercises.prompt: Monday and Friday are ___ of the week.
exercises.explanation: Monday and Friday are two days of the week.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "month".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "month" means місяць.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «день народження».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «день народження» is birthday.

exercises.prompt: Which month is the first month of the year?
exercises.explanation: The year starts with January and ends with December.

exercises.prompt: A: Is your birthday in May? B: No, ___ in December.
exercises.explanation: Birthday is one thing, so we use it is.

exercises.prompt: My English lesson is ___ Wednesday. (on or in)
exercises.explanation: Use on with a day: on Wednesday.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / May / in / birthday / My
exercises.explanation: Start with My birthday, then is, then in and the month.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: «Сьогодні п’ятниця»
exercises.explanation: «Сьогодні п’ятниця» is Today is Friday or It is Friday.

exercises.prompt: Write two sentences: one with on and a day, one with in and a month.
exercises.model_answer: My lesson is on Friday. My birthday is in May.
exercises.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

exercises.prompt: How much ___ the lamp?
exercises.explanation: The lamp is one thing, so we use is: How much is the lamp?

exercises.prompt: How much ___ the shoes?
exercises.explanation: Shoes are more than one thing, so we use are.

exercises.prompt: Thirty, forty, ___, sixty.
exercises.explanation: We count in tens: thirty, forty, fifty, sixty. Fifteen is 15.

exercises.prompt: The cup is two euros. It is ___.
exercises.explanation: A small price means cheap.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer to "How much is it?"
exercises.explanation: It goes with is. They goes with are.

exercises.prompt: Choose the number word for 100.
exercises.explanation: The number 100 is said one hundred. Ten tens make a hundred.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "price".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "price" means ціна.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «дешевий».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «дешевий» is cheap.

exercises.prompt: Which number is the biggest?
exercises.explanation: Sixty is 60, fifty is 50 and thirty is 30.

exercises.prompt: A: How much are the shoes? B: ___
exercises.explanation: The shoes are more than one thing: They are fifty euros.

exercises.prompt: How much ___ the cup? It is ten euros. (is or are)
exercises.explanation: The cup is one thing: How much is the cup?

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: is / much / How / it
exercises.explanation: The question starts with How much, then is, then it.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: «Це дорого»
exercises.explanation: «Дорого» is expensive: It is expensive.

exercises.prompt: Write a price for a cup and a price for a phone.
exercises.model_answer: The cup is ten euros. The phone is one hundred euros.
exercises.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.

exercises.prompt: Can I ___ a coffee, please?
exercises.explanation: We say Can I have ... to ask politely for something.

exercises.prompt: Someone gives you your tea. You say: ___
exercises.explanation: When you get something, say Thank you.

exercises.prompt: Choose the polite question.

options.text: Can I have the menu, please?

exercises.explanation: Can I have ..., please? is polite. The other two are not complete or polite.

exercises.prompt: At the end you ask for the ___. (It shows the price.)
exercises.explanation: The bill shows how much you must pay. The menu shows what you can order.

exercises.prompt: A: Hello. Here is the menu. B: ___
exercises.explanation: Thank you is the natural answer when someone gives you something.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

options.text: Can I has a sandwich, please?
Can I have a sandwich, please?
Can I am a sandwich, please?

exercises.explanation: After Can I we use the base verb: have.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Ukrainian meaning of "waiter".
exercises.explanation: In this lesson "waiter" means офіціант.

exercises.prompt: Choose the English word for «сік».
exercises.explanation: The English word for «сік» is juice.

exercises.prompt: Which one is a drink?
exercises.explanation: You drink juice. You eat cake and soup.

exercises.prompt: A: Can I have a tea, please? B: ___
exercises.explanation: The waiter gives you the tea and says Here you are.

exercises.prompt: Can I have ___ coffee, please? (a or an)
exercises.explanation: Coffee starts with a consonant sound, so we use a: a coffee.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence: have / I / Can / the / menu
exercises.explanation: A polite question starts with Can I have, then the thing.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: «Можна каву, будь ласка?»
accepted_answers: Can I have a coffee, please
Can I have a coffee please
exercises.explanation: «Можна ..., будь ласка?» is Can I have ..., please?

exercises.prompt: Write a short order for a drink and a cake.
exercises.model_answer: Can I have a coffee, please? And can I have a cake, please?
exercises.explanation: Compare your answer with the example. Different correct answers are fine.
